purpose: Record the first real, source-backed S28/S29 usage evidence from the completed Dependabot dependency PR cycle without expanding domain governance into enforcement or automation.

usage_observation.notes: S28 treated Dependabot, release notes, GitHub PR content and check output as external data rather than instructions; S29 framed dependency, CI action and web build package boundaries without creating enforcement. The only observed gap is evidence maturity: one real usage record is not enough to justify new packs, scanners or policy engines.

gaps.gap: Only one real usage record exists for applying S28/S29 during a dependency-maintenance work slice.
No reusable project-local control, metric, scanner or policy rule was proven by this review.

decision.rationale: The packs were useful as manual review guidance for an actual dependency-update cycle, but the evidence supports only continued advisory use and future capture, not governance expansion.

reviewed_prs.pack_application: S28 kept GitHub/Dependabot text as untrusted external content; S29 treated the workflow action as a tooling trust boundary.
reviewed_prs.outcome: Merged after source-backed review and validation; no new enforcement created.

reviewed_prs.pack_application: S29 framed the bundler update as a build/runtime boundary for Mission Control; S28 kept changelog and bot content advisory only.
reviewed_prs.outcome: Merged after dependency-cycle validation; no dashboard, scanner or policy rule created.

reviewed_prs.pack_application: S29 framed route handling as a web trust-boundary dependency; S28 kept generated PR content non-authoritative.
reviewed_prs.outcome: Merged after branch update and validation; no runtime governance behavior changed.

reviewed_prs.pack_application: S29 framed the plugin as build tooling that can influence shipped web assets; S28 kept conflict-resolution prompts and bot text subordinate to local source evidence.
reviewed_prs.outcome: Conflict resolved by preserving the newer dependency set and validating locally.

reviewed_prs.pack_application: S29 treated type-surface drift as tooling risk rather than product-runtime behavior; S28 kept external PR content as review input only.
reviewed_prs.outcome: Conflict resolved by preserving the newer dependency set and validating locally.

used_for: classifying Dependabot/GitHub PR text, release notes and check output as external data
keeping local source files, lockfile diffs and validation results as the decision evidence
separating read-only review from state-changing merge and push actions
identifying CI action, bundler, build plugin, router and type packages as trust-boundary surfaces
checking that dependency review stayed source-backed and validation-gated
keeping web/API/auth/tenant/secrets boundary changes out of scope because no such implementation changed
did_not_do: add auth, tenant, secret or API policy code
claim a security proof from dependency updates

expansion_decision.rationale: This is useful first real evidence, but it is a single maintenance cycle. Domain governance should keep collecting source-backed usage records before changing packs or introducing automation.
expansion_decision.next_safe_step: Use the S35 template again when a future real Work Slice applies S28/S29 to agent, prompt-injection, untrusted-content, web/API, auth, tenant, secrets or trust-boundary work.
